perspective: Adversarial cross-pipeline verification of handoffs, ownership, status authority, permissions, visibility, external actors, and approval/order claims using all three transcripts as primary evidence and Markdown artifacts as provisional summaries.

findings.claim: Mayra -> Laura is a confirmed operational handoff for student appointments.
evidence: Laura transcript lines 46-50: Mayra receives faculty requests, enters the spreadsheet, and it then comes to Laura to process.
Laura transcript lines 69-80: Mayra enters request fields; Laura adds missing fields and begins screening/workflow.
Mayra transcript lines 44-52: Mayra starts the request and collects fields required for Laura and Daisy.
findings.risk: The shared spreadsheet is the practical transport, but no authoritative handoff event, acceptance state, or exception contract is confirmed.
findings.recommendation: Model submission as a handoff with explicit received/returned states; do not infer acceptance from row creation.

findings.claim: Laura -> Finance/Daisy is confirmed for records Laura verifies in Oracle, but only the downstream costing trigger is established.
evidence: Laura transcript lines 120-130: after Laura verifies the Oracle record, Daisy can filter verified items and perform costing.
Daisy transcript lines 1028-1049: Finance checks chartfields, resolves funding issues, updates the worksheet, and marks its work with status/date/initials.
findings.risk: The evidence does not establish that every Laura-managed appointment enters Finance, who formally accepts the handoff, or whether Finance status is authoritative outside the worksheet.
findings.recommendation: Define a verified-to-finance handoff contract scoped by appointment/assignment.

findings.claim: Finance can hand work back upstream for funding and activity clarification; Finance also performs termination-side updates, but final authority is unresolved.
evidence: Daisy transcript lines 1028-1049: Finance verifies chartfields, discusses missing funds, changes chartfields, and rechecks them.
Daisy transcript lines 892-922: Finance maintains an active summary, terminates entries it identifies as ended, and asks Mayra/Laura to confirm uncertain appointments.
Laura transcript lines 1087-1096: student termination requests should flow through Mayra to Laura; Laura acts from the spreadsheet.
findings.risk: Finance worksheet edits and Laura Oracle changes overlap; canonical termination/status authority is not stated.
findings.recommendation: Assign separate authority for HR lifecycle, Finance costing lifecycle, and cross-team confirmation.

findings.claim: External actors are pipeline participants: faculty provide/confirm requests and funding, students complete screening/signing/preboarding, hiring authorities sign, and an HR approver controls the Oracle queue.
evidence: Mayra transcript lines 12-35 and 44-52: faculty provide renewal/new-appointment information; Mayra chases nonresponses.
Laura transcript lines 78-89 and 252-260: students complete screening and sign DocuSign offers; Laura chases them.
Laura transcript lines 87-89 and 541-548: Chanel/Dr. Sarkar sign hiring-authority letters.
Laura transcript lines 120-130: Oracle entries wait in an HR approval queue before verification/costing.
findings.risk: External completion events and queue outcomes are represented as statuses, but their source/reconciliation mechanisms are unspecified.
findings.recommendation: Treat external actors and Oracle approval as boundary events with provenance and reconciliation.

findings.claim: Status fields are operational coordination markers, not proven authoritative state machines.
evidence: Laura transcript lines 78-80, 85-103, 114-130: Laura filters and changes screening, stage, Oracle, check, and verified fields.
Laura transcript lines 95-109: Laura and an HR colleague both work the sheet; initials and blue highlighting are local tracking.
Mayra transcript lines 337-352: Mayra says Laura should change Laura statuses; Mayra should view them because she lacks Oracle access.
Daisy transcript lines 1035-1049: Finance uses green/in-progress and a later unclear status with date and initials.
findings.risk: Multiple editors, personal colors, and the unclear Finance terminal status weaken authority claims.
findings.recommendation: Do not treat colors, initials, or free-form statuses as authority; resolve Finance terminal status before implementation.

findings.claim: Permissions and visibility are unresolved; current sensitive-data practice conflicts with proposed universal visibility.
evidence: Daisy transcript lines 516-524: Finance reconciliation data is sensitive; Mayra and Laura do not have access.
Daisy transcript lines 529-536: Ian proposes everybody can see everything while only some can edit; Daisy agrees to the proposal.
Laura transcript lines 887-901: Ian proposes role-gated changes with broad view access and defers advanced permissions.
findings.risk: The broad-visibility proposal is not approved policy and would expose finance-sensitive data if implemented literally.
findings.recommendation: Preserve least-privilege visibility; require explicit owner approval for cross-domain views and masking.

findings.claim: Laura-before-Daisy is supported for the verified-to-costing path, but generic approval/order claims are assumptions or overstatements.
evidence: Laura transcript lines 122-130: Daisy acts after Laura verifies the Oracle appointment.
Laura transcript lines 1062-1082: Laura says there is not really an approval for student-hiring changes; Mayra headcount is already approved with Dr. Sarkar.
Mayra transcript lines 444-462: Mayra enters chartfields to get started; Daisy performs substantive chartfield/distribution work.
Mayra artifact lines 23-31 and 90: Laura-before-Daisy and related order details are explicitly open/assumed.
findings.risk: A universal approval gate would conflate headcount approval, hiring-authority signature, Oracle HR approval, Laura verification, and Finance checks.
findings.recommendation: Represent those gates separately and preserve the assumed label where evidence is second-hand.

findings.claim: Change requests are a cross-pipeline loop with confirmed audit need, but requester, approver, and executor vary by change type.
evidence: Laura transcript lines 780-805 and 851-860: post-completion changes require a new offer letter and Oracle amendment.
Laura transcript lines 1025-1058: funding changes need Daisy visibility and auditable history.
Laura transcript lines 1087-1096: student requests should route through Mayra to Laura, although faculty bypass occurs.
Mayra transcript lines 214-226: late job-code changes require restricted overwrite access.
findings.risk: Job-code, funding, termination, and faculty/staff changes have different owners and effects; one generic loop is unsafe.
findings.recommendation: Use typed change-request classes with requester, affected assignment, reviewers, executor, downstream reprocessing, and immutable before/after values.

missing_or_ambiguous: No authoritative system or formal acceptance event is identified for worksheet handoffs.
Exact Finance completion status is unclear in Daisy transcript lines 1042-1049 ("page" may be transcription error); do not normalize it to "paid".
Canonical authority for termination, active/inactive status, and Finance edits versus Laura Oracle changes is unresolved.
Whether Finance costing applies to every student appointment or primarily faculty/staff/stipend cases is unresolved; Daisy examples are faculty-focused (Daisy transcript lines 83-101, 126-189).
Permission policy is unresolved: Finance sensitivity conflicts with proposed broad read visibility.
Oracle HR approval is distinct from business/headcount approval; owner and transition semantics are unspecified.
External-event provenance, reconciliation, retry, and stale-status handling are undefined.

source_coverage.role: Provisional cross-pipeline summary checked against transcripts.
